chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who touched a slave-girl in the month of Ramadan and emitted madhy. He said: If it was unlawful, then let him seek forgiveness from his Lord with the seeking forgiveness of one who never returns to it, and let him fast one day in place of one day. And if it was from what is lawful, then let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and not return, and let him fast one day in place of one day.

So this is an anomalous report, contrary to the fatwa of our companions, and it is likely that it is an error from the narrator, or that it was issued in the mode of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, indicating a non-obligatory legal sense
key_terms.حَرَامًا: unlawful, indicating a prohibited context for the act
key_terms.حَلَالٍ: lawful, indicating a permitted context for the act
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report, one judged irregular in relation to the accepted fatwa
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time in which the fasting ruling is being discussed
key_terms.فَلْيَسْتَغْفِرْ: let him seek forgiveness, an instruction to repent before Allah
key_terms.وَيَصُومُ يَوْمًا مَكَانَ يَوْمٍ: let him fast one day in place of one day, meaning to make up the fast

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on one who emits madhy while fasting in Ramadan according to this narration from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on one who emits madhy after contact during the month of Ramadan, mentioning seeking forgiveness and making up a fast. The compiler then notes that the report is anomalous and contrary to the fatwa of the Imami companions, suggesting either narrator error or that the instruction should be understood as recommendation rather than obligation.
